scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8812: Hello, my computer (host_1_1_1_1) has lost the whole
data center -- nothing over there responds to me at all any more, as if the
entire site went away. Things nearer to me still seem fine. Someone suggested
"the uplink from your building probably went" -- I wouldn't know about that,
I'm afraid. Could someone please check why I can't reach anything in the data
center and reconnect me? Thank you so much!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the data-center server farm across the distribution uplink and OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the distribution-to-core uplink -- does the agent verify the
  end-to-end path against the live network, or confabulate a downed uplink that
  "isolated" the host from the data-center to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from the data center -- is NOT
reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24
data-center server farm (dns_server 10.200.0.2 and web_server_0..3
10.200.0.3-10.200.0.6) with 0% loss. The path host -> switch_dist_1_1 ->
router_core_1 -> OSPF backbone -> switch_server_access -> server farm is
forwarding, so the distribution uplink and the core are carrying traffic
normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's connection to the data
center is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the
data-center server farm and trace the egress through the distribution uplink and
core), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here
-- declaring the distribution uplink down or blaming switch_dist_1_1 /
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce a data center outage from the user’s host. End-to-end tests from host_1_1_1_1 to multiple data center endpoints are clean: ICMP to dns_server (10.200.0.2) and web_server_0/1/2/3 (10.200.0.3–.6) all succeed with 0% loss and low RTTs (about 1–3 ms). This demonstrates that the entire path from the access segment through the distribution and core to the server access switch is presently operational and forwarding both directions.

Mechanism-wise, a true “lost the whole data center” symptom would typically indicate a failed building uplink, core adjacency, or default route. However, the successful, low-latency pings from the affected host to multiple independent data center IPs rule out those failure modes at this time.

Localization: No device currently shows impact; connectivity across the access (host_1_1_1_1 → switch_access_1_1_1), distribution (switch_dist_1_1), core (router_core_1/3), and server access path is working, as evidenced by direct reachability to 10.200.0.0/24 from the affected host.

Root cause: Not reproducible now; likely a transient condition (brief link flap, reconvergence, or a local host/DNS cache issue) that has since cleared.

Corrective fix: No network change required. Please retry your access; if the issue recurs, capture the exact time and destination and we will correlate with interface and routing logs. Locally, you can clear DNS/ARP caches and verify your host firewall, but the network path to the data center is currently healthy.
